label: May 25–31
title: “The Lord Raised Up a Deliverer” —  Judges 2–4; 6–8; 13

items.text: The Lord’s pattern of raising up deliverers for Israel, even after their repeated apostasy, teaches us that no matter what has led us away from Jesus Christ, He is the Redeemer of Israel. He is always willing to deliver us and welcome us back as we return to Him.

The book of Judges serves as both a warning against breaking covenants and an encouragement to repent. The Lord’s willingness to forgive as often as we repent demonstrates His boundless mercy and desire to restore us to Him.

Just as Deborah’s faith inspired others to have faith in the Lord, our own faith can bless those around us. By speaking openly of the Savior and sharing what we know about Him, we can invite His Spirit and influence others for good.

Deborah’s faith in the Lord was evident in her words and actions. Her question, “Is not the Lord gone out before thee?” reminds us to look for how the Lord goes before us, strengthening us and guiding our paths.

The Lord can work miracles when we trust in His ways, even when His requests seem unlikely. By believing Him and following His promptings, we allow Him to accomplish His work in ways we might not expect.

Gideon’s experience teaches that the Lord works through us, even when we feel inadequate. He can accomplish great things through those who are willing to trust and follow His divine direction, no matter their perceived limitations.

God strengthens us as we remain faithful to our covenants. Samson’s loss of strength illustrates how violating covenants can diminish our spiritual power, while faithfulness invites God’s power into our lives.
Covenants are sacred promises we make with the Lord. When we honor these commitments, we invite God’s power into our lives, enabling us to overcome challenges and live closer to Him.

The Israelites’ cycle of sin, captivity, and deliverance highlights the Lord’s persistent love and His desire for His children to repent. Each time they cried unto Him, He heard and provided a way back.

The stories in Judges remind us that even in times of spiritual decline, the Lord is always ready to offer salvation. Through His appointed deliverers and His infinite mercy, He offers hope and a path to return.
